```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE
)

library(tidyverse)
library(plotly)

data("ny_noaa", package = "p8105.datasets")

weather_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  filter(
    id == "USC00300055",
    date >= as.Date("2010-01-01"),
    date < as.Date("2011-01-01")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    month = factor(
      as.integer(format(date, "%m")),
      levels = 1:12,
      labels = month.abb
    )
  ) |>
  select(id, date, month, tmax, tmin) |>
  arrange(date)

weather_check =
  weather_df |>
  summarise(
    n_observations = n(),
    n_dates = n_distinct(date),
    missing_tmax = sum(is.na(tmax)),
    missing_tmin = sum(is.na(tmin)),
    reversed_temperatures = sum(tmin > tmax, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

stopifnot(
  weather_check$n_observations == 365,
  weather_check$n_dates == 365,
  weather_check$missing_tmax == 0,
  weather_check$missing_tmin == 0,
  weather_check$reversed_temperatures == 0
)

monthly_df =
  weather_df |>
  group_by(month) |>
  summarise(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    mean_tmin = mean(tmin, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("mean_"),
    names_to = "measure",
    values_to = "temperature"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    measure = recode(
      measure,
      mean_tmax = "Daily maximum",
      mean_tmin = "Daily minimum"
    ),
    hover_text = paste0(
      "Month: ", month,
      "<br>Measure: ", measure,
      "<br>Monthly mean: ", round(temperature, 1), " °C"
    )
  )

theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
)
```

-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### How to read this dashboard

[Return to the homepage](index.html) · [Resume](resume.html)

The data come from `ny_noaa` in the `p8105.datasets` package. This dashboard
uses station **USC00300055** from **January 1 to December 31, 2010**. I chose
this station-year because it has a complete year of daily maximum and minimum
temperature observations. All three plots use this same station and year.

There are **`r weather_check$n_observations` observations** on
**`r weather_check$n_dates` distinct dates**. The maximum-temperature and
minimum-temperature variables contain **`r weather_check$missing_tmax`** and
**`r weather_check$missing_tmin`** missing values, respectively. There are
**`r weather_check$reversed_temperatures`** records with a minimum temperature
greater than the maximum temperature. No observations were removed or sampled
after selecting the station and year.

The original temperature fields are stored as character values in tenths of
degrees Celsius. I converted them to numeric values and divided by 10; all
temperature axes below use **degrees Celsius (°C)**. Monthly averages give
each observed day equal weight at this one station. These plots describe one
station-year and do not estimate a statewide average or a long-term climate trend.

Hover over a plot to inspect values. Drag to zoom; double-click to reset the
view. On the line plot, click a legend item to show or hide that series.

### Monthly mean daily temperatures — line plot

```{r monthly-line}
monthly_plot =
  ggplot(
    monthly_df,
    aes(
      x = month,
      y = temperature,
      color = measure,
      group = measure,
      text = hover_text
    )
  ) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#D55E00", "#0072B2")) +
  labs(
    x = "Month (2010)",
    y = "Monthly mean temperature (°C)",
    color = NULL
  )

ggplotly(monthly_plot, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(
    margin = list(l = 75, r = 25, b = 100, t = 20),
    legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0.2, y = -0.2)
  ) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE)
```

Row {data-height=500}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Daily minimum versus maximum temperature — scatterplot

```{r daily-scatter}
scatter_df =
  weather_df |>
  mutate(
    hover_text = paste0(
      "Date: ", date,
      "<br>Minimum: ", tmin, " °C",
      "<br>Maximum: ", tmax, " °C"
    )
  )

scatter_plot =
  ggplot(scatter_df, aes(x = tmin, y = tmax, text = hover_text)) +
  geom_point(color = "#0072B2", alpha = 0.65, size = 1.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Daily minimum temperature (°C)",
    y = "Daily maximum temperature (°C)"
  )

ggplotly(scatter_plot, tooltip = "text") |>
  layout(margin = list(l = 75, r = 25, b = 75, t = 20)) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE)
```

Row {data-height=500}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Daily maximum temperatures by month — boxplot

```{r monthly-box}
box_plot =
  ggplot(weather_df, aes(x = month, y = tmax)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#56B4E9", alpha = 0.7, width = 0.65) +
  labs(
    x = "Month (2010)",
    y = "Daily maximum temperature (°C)"
  )

ggplotly(box_plot) |>
  layout(margin = list(l = 75, r = 25, b = 75, t = 20)) |>
  config(displaylogo = FALSE)
```

Row {data-height=180}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Notes and sources

The line plot shows monthly means, the scatterplot shows individual days,
and the boxplot summarizes within-month variation in daily maximum temperature.
The two temperature series are plotted on the same Celsius scale. The
boxplot summarizes the observations rather than plotting a monthly average.

Data: `p8105.datasets::ny_noaa`.
[Package documentation](https://p8105.github.io/p8105.datasets/reference/ny_noaa.html).
